🛠️ Endpoints just got faster and safer with BullMQ"
""
"Yesterday, I explored message queueing with BullMQ and integrated it practically into my codebase."
""
"Heavy CPU / API calls are now handled as non-blocking background jobs, while users get immediate responses for what truly matters."
""
"I applied this mainly to workflows where users shouldn’t have to wait:"
"	•	Notifications"
"	•	Emails"
"	•	Scheduled tasks"
""
"⸻"
""
"Why this mattered beyond speed"
""
"Queues didn’t just improve response times, they introduced predictable execution and controlled failure."
""
"With BullMQ:"
"	•	User requests return immediately"
"	•	Side-effects run asynchronously with retry guarantees"
"	•	Failures are isolated, observable, and recoverable (instead of crashing requests)"
""
"This means my system now favors at-least-once delivery, idempotent jobs, and automatic retries — increasing reliability at scale."
""
"⸻"
""
"Scheduling without CRON fragility"
""
"BullMQ’s scheduling goes beyond traditional CRON jobs:"
"	•	Jobs are stateful and persisted"
"	•	Execution is distributed-safe"
"	•	No single scheduler bottleneck"
""
"A practical use case:"
"When a conversation is created, I schedule its expiration 24 hours ahead."
"Once the time elapses, a background job expires the conversation and emits realtime updates to the frontend — without polling or blocking."
""
"⸻"
""
"What users no longer wait for"
"	•	Email delivery"
"	•	Notification fan-out"
"	•	Expensive side-effects"
""
"Those run in workers with controlled concurrency, backpressure, and retry policies."
""
"If load increases, I scale workers — not endpoints."
""
"⸻"
""
"The real ideology"
""
"Make users wait only for absolute must-haves."
"Everything else becomes observable, retryable background work."
""
"This approach scales cleanly in distributed systems and protects core APIs under load."
""
"⸻"
""
"Next up: caching — pushing data as close to users as possible (L3 where feasible), and coordinating cache invalidation through background jobs instead of guesswork."

Switching From localStorage to Redux Persist for Better UX"
""
"We’ve all been in that situation where you update your profile or edit a post… and the old information stays there for a few seconds — sometimes until you refresh or even log out."
""
"That’s not a great user experience."
""
"I realized that relying on localStorage to hold and display user information makes issues like stale data almost unavoidable. That’s one of the major reasons I switched to Redux Persist for storing user state."
""
"Redux Persist works almost the same way as localStorage after setup, but with one important advantage:"
""
"✅ Automatic state updates after invalidation"
""
"When data changes, Redux Persist rehydrates your store with fresh values automatically. No refreshing. No logging out. No confusion for the user."
""
"The result?"
""
"🎯 Smoother user experience"
""
"🎯 Instant reflection of updates"
""
"🎯 More confidence that the app responded to their action"
""
"Happy users = better retention."
"And users shouldn’t have to wonder whether your app actually “heard” them."
""
"I’m sure there are many other ways to improve user experience that I’ve not discovered yet, and I’m always open to learning."
""

""

""

""

""

""
"Branding: A brand isn’t just what people see; it’s how they feel about your product. Communicating the right emotions is key."
""
"Marketing Fundamentals: Define your market positioning and unique value proposition. Conduct a SWOT analysis, explore channels, and develop a detailed marketing plan."
""
"Market Analysis: Segment your market and study competitors. This helps you avoid wasted time, resources, and bootstrapped energy."

""
"Legals"
""
"Register and license your business early. It builds credibility and protects your work."
""
""

""
"Understand how your business makes and spends money."
""
"Financial Planning: Develop projections and a break-even analysis. Create a budget and identify key financial metrics to track."
""
"Funding Strategies: Explore your options, whether it’s bootstrapping, venture capital, or grants, and choose what fits your stage of growth."

How to Deliver the Perfect Pitch ✨"
""
"Last week, I had the opportunity to pitch for a share of the ₦500m budget allocated to creating new income streams within the Tenece Professional Services Group."
""
"With two weeks to prepare, my goal was to find gaps that could still generate solid revenue and strengthen our position in the market. That part came naturally — research, data, and numbers."
""
"But here’s what most people miss: pitching isn’t just about what you say, it’s about how you deliver it. Many people have great ideas but fail to structure their thoughts clearly."
""
"Here are the 5 steps I used to clarify my points:"
""
"1. Start with the goal : Outline the company’s objective (in this case, a 41% increase in net revenue)."
"2. Present the gap : Identify where new opportunities lie and why they matter now."
"3. Show the value : Back every idea with numbers and clear impact."
"4. Make it relatable : Use real examples and practical scenarios to connect your idea to results."
"5. End with clarity : Summarize your key point and state your ask confidently."
""
"And just like that, in 5 minutes I was able to justify why 23% of the budget should go to Genesys Tech Hub, focusing on real solutions to real problems that could drive new income streams and match the company’s growth goals."
""
"A good pitch isn’t about speaking more; it’s about speaking clearly, with structure and purpose."

🛠️ The Prisma Migration Drift That Almost Cost Me My Job!"
""
"Migration drift had always been a black box to me, until a few weeks ago."
""
"An incident occurred, someone on the team created a couple of migrations, and somehow, the local migration files vanished. Everyone claimed they didn’t have them. 🥲"
""
"As the Backend Team Lead, I needed a solution—fast. No one could make any database edits without resetting it, and at this point, features were already weeks behind. My supervisor’s patience was running out."
""
"After a few hours of digging, I finally stumbled on the perfect article."
""
"Here are the 5 steps I took to recover the missing migration files:"
"	1.	Fetched the missing migration names from the database’s _prisma_migrations table."
"	2.	Recreated the missing migration files manually, covering as much schema info as possible."
"	3.	Recalculated a checksum for each new migration file."
"	4.	Updated the _prisma_migrations table with the new checksum values."
"	5.	Ran a fresh migration to resolve all previous drifts and re-align the state."
""
"This entire experience taught me some important lessons:"
"	•	Prisma tracks migration integrity using the _prisma_migrations table."
"	•	Always read CLI messages carefully—especially ones related to schema or drift. Never reset blindly."
"	•	Backups are life. One wrong step with a production database could mean irreversible damage—and probably your job."
""
"That’s how I fixed a critical migration drift issue under pressure, and what I learned from it as a Backend Lead. If you ever run into something similar, I hope this post finds you in time."

"What is Global State Management (GSM)?"
""
"GSM means storing data that needs to be shared across the entire application. In the past, I relied on Props and Context API, but now I’m upskilling with Redux for better scalability and efficiency."

"Key GSM Concepts :"

" - Complex Applications : When you have multiple interconnected components that need to access the same data. "
" - Shared Data: One data needed across different parts of your app"
" - Frequent Update: When the same state is updated by various components, centralizing it helps keep data organized"

"What Is a Heap Allocation Error?"
""
"This error occurs when your application runs out of memory while trying to allocate space in the heap, a region of memory used to store dynamically allocated data. It’s commonly caused by two scenarios:"
"📍 Memory Leaks: When memory isn’t released after being used, leading to exhaustion over time."
"📍 ⁠Limited RAM: When the system’s allocated memory is insufficient for the app’s demands."
""
""
"How It Happened"
""
"The root cause of my issue was insufficient RAM. After pushing a major update, the system’s demands increased, and with the tight memory limits on my #AWSLightsail instance, it couldn’t start up successfully. This triggered the dreaded heap allocation error, temporarily taking production offline—a stressful and eye-opening experience."
""
""
"Temporary Fix"
""
"To address the issue quickly, I upgraded my Lightsail instance to one with more RAM. This provided the system with enough memory to start up and run smoothly, allowing production to recover while I investigated further."
""
""
"Permanent Fix"
""
"If a memory leak is identified as the root cause, solving it requires a thorough debugging and optimization process:"
"	1.	Profiling the Application: Use tools like Node.js Heap Profiler or VisualVM to monitor memory usage and identify leaks."
"	2.	Fixing Leaks: Look for objects that are no longer referenced but aren’t being garbage collected. Refactor code to ensure proper memory management."
"	3.	Stress Testing: Simulate high-traffic scenarios to confirm the issue is resolved and the app can handle its workload."
""
"For a detailed guide on debugging memory leaks, I recommend this great article - https://lnkd.in/dCkw4Sqe"

""
"How to Identify a Memory Leak"
""
"Detecting a memory leak often starts with observing memory usage patterns:"
"📍 If memory usage continuously grows without stabilizing, even when traffic decreases, a leak is likely."
"📍 ⁠Tools like Chrome DevTools, Heapdump, or PM2 monitoring can provide valuable insights into memory usage trends."

Burning Platform: From Render to AWS 🎚️"
""
"Making the switch from Render to AWS was a game-changer, but it came with a steep learning curve. Here’s how I tackled the migration, what worked, and the key lessons I learned along the way."
""
"I needed to quickly choose the best AWS services for a Container Registry, Orchestration, Virtual Server, Cloud Object Storage, Postgres DB, and CI/CD. Here’s what I went with:"
""
"1.	AWS ECR (Elastic Container Registry)"
"2.	AWS ECS (Elastic Container Service)"
"3.	AWS EC2 (Elastic Compute Cloud)"
"4.	AWS S3 (Simple Storage Service)"
"5.	AWS RDS (Relational Database Service)"
"6.	GitHub Actions"
""
"How it all fits together:"
""
"AWS ECR:"
"Similar to Docker Hub, it served as my container registry."
""
"•	I created a container image and pushed it to ECR."
""
"AWS ECS:"
"This was my orchestration service—this part was tricky."
""
"•	I created a Cluster and Task Definition."
"•	The Cluster then spun up an EC2 instance based on the specs I provided."
"•	I set up a Daemon Service to create tasks using the Task Definition."
""
"AWS EC2:"
"EC2 served as the virtual server."
""
"•	The Cluster automatically created an instance for me."
"•	The tasks generated snapshots of my container here."
"•	I could then access the app from this EC2 instance."
""
"AWS S3:"
"Used for cloud object storage."
""
"•	I uploaded my environment files here (using SSE encryption) because AWS Secrets Manager was a bit pricey."
"•	I had to add an S3 permission policy to my ECS task definition so it could access these files."
""
"AWS RDS:"
"Set up a free-tier Postgres database here. Easy enough!"
""
"GitHub Actions:"
"My go-to for CI/CD."
""
"•	I used an AWS.yml file based on the GitHub docs and customized it."
"•	The Task Definition JSON file was added to the root directory, and I updated all the parameters."
""
"How it works now:"
""
"1.	On every push, my code is containerized and pushed to ECR."
"2.	The Task Definition is updated in ECS."
"3.	A new task is created based on the latest definition."
"4.	I can access the updated deployment via the EC2 public IP. 🥳"
""
"Common Mistakes to Avoid:"
""
"1.	Set Network Mode to “host” in the Task Definition if your VPC subnet is public; awsvpc only works in a private subnet."
"2.	S3 won’t work unless you add the right permissions in your Task Definition."
"3.	The Task Definition specs must match the EC2 instance specs."
"4.	Set the minimum task count to 0 in your Service settings—this allows CI/CD deployments to replace the running task."
""
"Final Tip: Always read the docs! Or, you know, just bookmark this post. ✌️"
""
